claims.text: Adjusting elemental composition in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune the magnetic transition temperature.
Adjusting elemental composition can enhance the magnetocaloric response of non-equiatomic HEAs.
Composition tuning affects magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior by altering local magnetic exchange interactions.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA has moderate magnetocaloric effects.
Systematically varying the ratios of magnetic elements is a method for tuning the alloy's behavior.
Local chemical ordering modulates magnetic exchange pathways.
Lattice distortions modulate magnetic exchange pathways.
Changing elemental ratios modifies the distribution of magnetic moments.
Changing elemental ratios modifies the strength of exchange interactions.
Modified magnetic-moment distributions and exchange interactions shift the critical magnetic transition temperature.
Modified magnetic-moment distributions and exchange interactions enhance the peak magnetic entropy change near the operational temperature.
An optimized composition will shift the magnetic transition temperature toward the required application range.
An optimized composition will produce a larger magnetic entropy change than the baseline composition.
Phase stability limits the useful range of composition tuning.
Solubility limits constrain the useful range of composition tuning.
Composition changes outside the phase-stability or solubility bounds may cause phase separation.
Composition changes outside the phase-stability or solubility bounds may degrade magnetic performance.
The magnitudes of the transition-temperature shift and magnetic-entropy-change enhancement depend on the specific alloy system.
